title: Jason Cohen on WP Engine: customer interviews, pricing, key metrics, and stepping down as CEO
summary: Jason Cohen explains how WP Engine started from 50 customer interviews and hit product-market fit via pricing changes and a 60-day money-back guarantee. He covers picking a leading "moment of value" metric over laggy MRR, when to raise VC, and his joy/skill/need framework for handing the CEO role to Heather.

principles.text: Validate a business with dozens of customer interviews about a real pain before building; the core promise can stay valid for over a decade.
Interviews must be directed; asking "do you like this feature" teaches you nothing because people just say yes.
principles.quote: if you're just asking like do you like this feature they're gonna say yeah sure that's you know that seems pretty good and you haven't learned a damn thing

principles.text: Pricing hinges on customers' mental price steps, not just willingness to pay. A tier jump they can't stomach in one shot blocks sales.
principles.quote: it probably is worth 50 but they can't do that in one shot like mentally that's not how they think about it

principles.text: When a free trial converts at 90%, you're losing revenue; charge up front with a longer money-back guarantee, which can raise sales.
principles.quote: we had a 90 percent 90 success rate after the two weeks so I was looking at going like well number one that's product Market fit when your trial is a 90 conversion rate

principles.text: Pick a leading metric at the moment customers get value; MRR is too laggy and multi-input to operate on (e.g. Netflix's 3+ DVDs queued).
principles.quote: if you imagine the customer moving through their Journey from like oh I found out about you in the website

principles.text: Use the joy, skill, need framework to decide your role; any two without the third is a trap (burnout, mediocrity, or building the wrong thing).
principles.quote: the joy skill trap is you love it and you're good at it so you do it and it feels good
